newsitem.title: UK: Bank of Ireland wins Lincolnshire pension mandate.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Ireland wins Lincolnshire pension mandate.

text.p: Bank of Ireland Asset Management (UK) has won the mandate to manage 27 million sterling for Lincolnshire County Council's pension fund, a county official said.
The funds will be actively invested in equities on Far East exchanges, excluding Japan, the official said.

This is Bank of Ireland Asset Management's second mandate for Lincolnshire Council, having managed 40 million sterling of European equities, excluding Britain, for the past two years, company managing director Francis Ellison told Reuters.
"We have an effective and well developed investment philosophy and a strong performance record in the region," he said.
Bank of Ireland Asset Management has made average returns in the Far East ex Japan of 27.3 percent over the past five years, Ellison said, handily beating the CAPS benchmark of 20.8 percent.
"We are a bottom-up stock picker and a value investor," he said.
Bank of Ireland Asset Management has 13.2 billion sterling under management.
A total of 44 firms bid to manage the 27 million stg, which had been invested in a variety of publicly traded investment vehicles, according to the Lincolnshire official.
